transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time, it's probably nothing too serious. 

But, well, what finally made me agree to come in is that I just... I don't seem to care about the things that used to keep me balanced. Like, I used to love the local sailing races, and I had this Saturday shift at the historical society that I always really enjoyed. Even just tinkering out in my woodshop... lately, it all just feels like a chore? I just keep putting those things off. 

I know it probably sounds a bit silly to come to a doctor just because I'm skipping my hobbies, but... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm in the right place and giving you the right information.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

Oh, um... no, not really sad. I mean, I have a good life, you know? I definitely don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself. I always try to keep a positive attitude about things. 

It's... it's really just that lack of drive I mentioned. I'm not crying or feeling miserable or anything like that. I'm still going to work and getting my projects done. I hope that's a helpful answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know.
Do you still enjoy things you used to find pleasurable, like eating your favorite foods or spending time with friends and family?

Well, I still eat fine and I love my family very much, of course. I don't want you to think I'm ignoring them or anything. It's just... I guess things don't give me that same spark they used to? 

Like, my wife and kids can be laughing at dinner, or I'll finish a really difficult project milestone at work... and I know those things should feel good. I want them to feel good. But mostly, I just feel kind of flat? A little removed from it all, maybe. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible husband or father. I really do try to be present for them. Is that the kind of information you were looking for?
How long have you been feeling this way, with things feeling like a chore and lacking that spark?

Well, um... I guess it's been a while now. I really don't want to make a big deal out of it, but... it started a little over a year ago. 

We were doing this big business readjustment at work, and... well, there was an accident with some scaffolding. I wasn't seriously hurt or anything, I promise! I don't want you to think I'm making a fuss over nothing. But, yeah, ever since then, things have just felt a bit different. 

I really hope I'm not overreacting by bringing it up. Does that timeline help you at all? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details so I'm not wasting your time.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge lately?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I'm anxious. I mean, everyone gets a little stressed with work deadlines and things, especially in my line of work, but... no, I don't really feel on edge. 

I actually try to pride myself on keeping a pretty level head. I definitely don't want to come across as a nervous wreck or anything like that! I handle pressure fine, I promise. It's really just that... that sort of detached feeling we talked about. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have that issue? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions correctly and giving you what you need.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

No, my weight has been pretty steady, actually. I mean, maybe a pound or two here and there around the holidays, but nothing major. I try to take good care of myself—eat right, stay active when I can. I definitely haven't let myself go or anything like that. 

I hope that's a good thing? I know sometimes stress can make people gain or lose a lot of weight, but I've managed to keep things pretty normal in that department. Is that what you were checking for?
Have you been having any trouble sleeping lately?

Well, um... I wouldn't call it major trouble, really. Most nights I can get to bed at a reasonable hour without any fuss. I try to keep a good, disciplined schedule. But... well, I guess sometimes I do wake up around two or three in the morning. And, um, my mind just sort of wanders back to that job site. Then I end up just lying there, kind of listening for every little sound instead of getting real rest. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a mess or anything! I still get up and do my job perfectly fine, I promise. It's just a little annoying, that's all, and I definitely don't want to blow it out of proportion. I'm sure plenty of people have restless nights, right? Is that the kind of detail you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering thoroughly for you.
Have you been feeling tired or having low energy lately?

Um, no, my energy levels are actually pretty good. I mean, even with those nights where I wake up like I mentioned, I always make sure to get right out of bed and get straight to my projects. I definitely don't let myself drag during the day. I'd really hate for anyone at work to think I'm slacking or that I can't handle my responsibilities, you know? 

I really pride myself on staying productive and keeping up with everything. So, no, no real fatigue or low energy. I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture and not, well, complaining about normal everyday tiredness that everyone gets. Am I doing okay with these answers? I just want to be as helpful as possible.
Do you often find yourself feeling guilty about things that have happened or things you've done?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I'm overwhelmed by it or anything. I mean, I know logically that I did my job. People keep telling me the controls were all in place and that nobody could have predicted it. But, um... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, there's just this... this sort of low-grade dread that kind of follows me around. 

And maybe a little bit of guilt, just... like I should have seen one more risk coming, you know? As a project manager, it's my job to see those things. But I really try not to let it consume me! I don't sit around crying about it or anything like that. I just... I want to make sure I'm doing things right and not letting anyone down. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding like I'm throwing a pity party or anything. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you had any thoughts about harming yourself or wishing you were dead?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, um, I would never do anything like that. I know things have been a little stressful, but I really do value my life, and I have way too many responsibilities to even entertain thoughts like that. 

I really try to keep a positive outlook, you know? I just want to move forward and get past all this. I'd hate for you to think I was, um, unstable or giving up. I'm fully committed to getting things back on track. That's a good thing to hear, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right impression.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

Um, no, not at all. If anything, I try to stay on top of everything and keep moving. I definitely haven't noticed any slowness in how I talk or walk, and no one at work has mentioned anything like that either. I always try to be sharp and responsive, especially in meetings. 

I really wouldn't want anyone to think I'm losing my edge or slowing down, you know? So, no, I'd say my pace is completely normal, maybe even a little brisk. I'm still keeping up with everything just fine. Is that what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering these the right way for you.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but no longer find interesting?

Well, um... I guess this is actually sort of what made me finally agree to come in and see you. I mean, I've always been a really active guy, and I definitely don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around doing nothing, but... lately, I just haven't had the same drive for my hobbies. 

The things that used to keep me balanced, you know? Like, um, the sailing races I usually do, or my Saturday shift at the historical society... even just tinkering out in my woodshop. I just don't really care about them right now, and I keep putting them off. Honestly, they just feel a bit like chores. 

I'm sure it's just a temporary rut, right? Everyone gets a little burned out sometimes. I really hope admitting that doesn't make me sound lazy or anything. I'm usually very on top of my schedule. Does that, um, answer your question okay?
Would you say that you have lost interest in almost all activities that you used to enjoy?

Oh, no, no, definitely not *all* of them. I mean, um, I don't want to make it sound like I'm just totally checked out of life or anything. I'm still very much engaged. Like, I still really care about my work—my projects are definitely still getting my full attention, and I'm still keeping up with all my responsibilities there. And, you know, I still like spending time with my family, or just watching a game on TV. 

It's really just those few specific hobbies I mentioned before that feel a bit heavy right now. I'm definitely not giving up on everything else. I always try to stay as active and involved as I can. Does that make sense? I just want to be sure I didn't give you the wrong idea a minute ago.
Would you say that this lack of interest in your hobbies has been present most of the day, every day?

Well, um... I wouldn't say every single day, no. I mean, I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around moping all the time. There are definitely days where I feel a bit more like my old self and think, "Hey, maybe I'll head out to the shop later." I might not always get out there, but the thought is there, you know? 

It's just... some days it's a little harder to muster up the energy for it. But I wouldn't say it's a constant, all-day, every-day kind of thing. I'm still trying my best to push through it and stay positive. I hope that's the kind of detail you need? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture without making it sound worse than it is.
Would you say that your lack of interest in hobbies is significantly impacting your daily life?

Well, um... I wouldn't say the hobby thing is ruining my day-to-day life or anything. But, um... I guess it has bled over a little bit into work? 

I mean, I'm still doing my job—I definitely don't want you to think I'm dropping the ball there, I take my career very seriously. But I have started... well, delegating some of the site visits that I really should be leading myself. And, um, if there's a client discussion coming up that I know might touch on... the accident... I've been kind of avoiding it, or just having one of my guys handle it instead. 

It does make me worry a little bit that I'm not giving the project the steady direction it really needs right now. I'm still managing everything, of course, just... maybe not quite as hands-on as I usually am. Does that answer what you were asking? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm being unprofessional or shirking my duties.
Would you say that your lack of interest in activities is accompanied by a depressed mood for most of the day?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I don't feel depressed or anything like that. I really want to make sure I'm being clear about that—I'm not walking around sad all day. 

I'm still generally pretty upbeat, and I try to keep a positive attitude, especially at work and around my family. It's just that little dip in motivation for the hobbies, like I mentioned. But as far as my actual mood goes, I feel pretty normal most of the time. I'm not down in the dumps or anything. I hope that's helpful? I just really don't want to give the impression that I'm depressed, because I'm definitely not.
Would you say that you feel depressed for most of the day?

Well, um... no, like I was just saying, I really don't feel depressed. I mean, I'm not sitting around crying or feeling miserable most of the day. I promise I'm not trying to hide anything, I just... I don't feel that way. 

I still have a lot to be thankful for, and I focus on that. I'm just maybe a little off my usual pace with the hobbies and some of the work stuff, but my mood itself is fine. I'm still me. Does that make sense? I just want to be sure I'm answering your questions the right way so you get an accurate picture.
Do you still enjoy things you used to find pleasurable, or has that changed recently?

Well, um... I guess that's actually the main reason I finally agreed to come in and talk to someone. I mean, I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, but... I just don't really care about the things that used to keep me balanced, you know? 

Like, I used to love the sailing races, and I had my Saturday shift at the historical society, which was always great. I even liked tinkering around in the woodshop. But lately... um... they all just feel like chores that I keep putting off. I know I should be doing them, and I feel a little guilty that I'm not, but the drive just isn't there right now. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or anything. I'm still keeping busy with other things, I promise. It's just those specific activities feel a bit heavy right now. Is that the kind of thing you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel like you're no longer getting pleasure from the activities you used to enjoy?

Well, yeah... I guess that's pretty much it. Like I was saying, it's just... I don't really get that same spark from them right now. 

The sailing, the historical society, the woodshop... they just feel like things on a to-do list that I keep putting off. I mean, I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing, because I'm definitely staying busy with work and everything else. It's just those specific things aren't bringing me the same joy they used to. 

I'm really trying to push through it, though. I hope I'm explaining this right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to understand what's going on.
Do you feel sad most of the day?

Well, um... no, I really don't. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I'm not feeling depressed or sad or anything like that. I'm really not. 

I don't want you to think I'm just sitting in a dark room feeling sorry for myself, because I'm not. I'm still going to work, I'm still getting things done... I'm just a little disconnected from my hobbies, that's all. But my mood itself is fine. I'm not sad. 

I hope I'm not repeating myself too much? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way so you know I'm still holding things together.
